walkthroughs.body_html:
The 19th century gave us Dickens, the Brontës, Hardy, Eliot and Austen.

Common GCSE texts include A Christmas Carol, Jane Eyre, Great Expectations, Frankenstein and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.

It was the era of the Industrial Revolution — soot, factories, child labour and huge inequality.

Britain was deeply class-divided. The wealthy lived in luxury; the poor crammed into workhouses and slums.

Most 19th-century novels use an omniscient narrator — a god-like voice that knows every character's thoughts.

Many follow the bildungsroman shape: a young hero grows up and learns life's lessons.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator's views are always the author's views.

The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
